timezone.name: Time zone
timezone.description: Current time anywhere, time zone conversions and daylight saving dates, from plain questions such as “time in tokyo”, “5pm ET to PT” or “when do the clocks change”.

diff.changesSame: From {date}, {zone} will have the same time as {base}.

dst.headline: {change} on {date}
dst.none: {zone} does not use daylight saving time
dst.statusYes: Yes, daylight saving time is in effect in {zone}
dst.statusNone: No, {zone} does not use daylight saving time

note.ambiguous: {term} was read as {zone}. It can also mean {alternatives}.
note.multiZone: {place} spans several time zones. Showing {zone}. Others include {alternatives}.
note.abbrSeason: {abbr} was read as {zone}, which is on {actual} at that time.
note.gapTime: {time} does not exist in {zone} on {date}, because the clocks go forward {amount}. Showing {shown} instead.
note.ambiguousTime: {time} happens twice in {zone} on {date}, because the clocks go back {amount}. Showing the first one.

homeZone.label: Home time zone
homeZone.description: Used when a question names no zone, such as “5pm ET” or “when does the time change”. Accepts an IANA zone, a city or an abbreviation. Blank uses the server's zone. Visitors' browsers replace it with their own zone unless “Use the visitor's time zone” is off.

timeFormat.label: Clock format
timeFormat.description: 12-hour, 24-hour, or follow the visitor's language when set to auto.

showSeconds.label: Show seconds
showSeconds.description: Show seconds on the live clock.

bareTriggers.label: Answer short queries
bareTriggers.description: Show the current time for two-word queries such as “tokyo time” or “london timezone”. Full questions such as “time in tokyo” always work.

browserZone.label: Use the visitor's time zone
browserZone.description: Let the browser add the visitor's own time and use their zone instead of the home time zone. Nothing is sent to the server.

onlineLookup.label: Look up other places online
onlineLookup.description: Find places that are not built in, such as “current time foster city” or “current time springfield il”, with the Open-Meteo geocoding service. Only the place name, and a country code when one is given, is sent, through degoog's outgoing connection. Off keeps every lookup on the server.
